author: reek
body: The adversarial half of let-arm scoping. `inner` is bound only inside the if-arm's let, and the arm has ended by the time `w + inner` runs, so the read is out of scope and this program must not compile.

author: reek
body: This rejects at the read, by name, with a line and a column. Getting there took removing the same aliasing bug from three places, and the diagnostic names which one is answering:

author: reek
body: The EMITTER used to answer, with `CDX2040: Unresolved call to 'inner' (redirected to __unresolved_trap)` -- a call the author never wrote -- because `env-bind-local` and `scope-add-local` both wrote their binding into the CALLER's scope, so the name was still bound when the arm ended and both the resolver and the checker let it through.

author: reek
body: Then the CHECKER answered (CDX2002), once the type environment stopped aliasing. Now the RESOLVER answers (CDX3002), which is the right phase: an out-of-scope name is a resolution question, and the resolver reaches it first. If this test ever reports CDX2002 or CDX2040 again, a scope fork has been lost -- the program is still rejected, so only the CODE tells you the discipline regressed.
